name: Dylan Tan
tagline: Hardware products from first sketch to global launch: design, sourcing, testing and go-to-market.
contact_line: Have a product to bring to market?
about:
I'm a hardware product manager and industrial designer. I take physical products from the first sketch through sourcing, testing and launch, at every scale from a one-off public fountain to a catalog of 34,000 SKUs.

Most recently at C.R. Laurence I ran the product lifecycle for CRL's highest-revenue architectural, railing and transaction hardware, led new product introduction, and directed the TurboFlex railing system with OnLevel in the Netherlands, from stress and wind-pressure testing through contract negotiations to a $35M initial rollout. Before that I led product development for more than 300 SKUs at Motech (Kitchen Bath Collection).

My background is hands-on. I studied 3-D Arts and Industrial Design at the University of Tennessee, I still prototype in metal, wood and concrete, model in Solidworks, Rhino and Blender, and build AI image pipelines in ComfyUI for marketing work.

experience.summary: End-to-end product lifecycle management for 34,000+ SKUs across CRL's highest-revenue B2B architectural, railing and transaction hardware. Led new product introduction (forecasting, market research, global vendor sourcing, ERP and go-to-market) and ran R&D pipelines of 6+ concurrent stage-gate products. Directed the ground-up development and launch of the TurboFlex railing system with OnLevel (Netherlands).

Owned product development start to finish for 300+ SKUs in B2B and B2C. Worked directly with factories on material sourcing and OEM delivery, and bridged engineering, marketing and outside stakeholders through launch.
Designed and developed products around customer experience, pairing an industrial design background with data analysis across cross-functional teams.
Led product development for an OEM badge company, from modular clip systems to B2B and B2C packaging.
Designed and fabricated luxury goods for city contracts and commercial clients, including public water fountains, sculptures and home furnishings.
Remote CAD work for American-made goods under a mentor: my introduction to production and modern manufacturing.
